object.label: Quantifying orthogonal barcodes for sequence census assays
object.description: Barcode-based sequence census assays can label biological features, but barcode design and technical noise complicate quantification. Assay-specific tools can be slow, memory-intensive, and hard to standardize across multimodal, multiplexing, and perturbation assays. kITE uniformly quantifies orthogonal barcode assays with fast, memory-efficient kallisto-bustools processing, while qcbc evaluates barcode-set quality and identifies ambiguity from shared subsequences, homopolymers, and low-diversity designs.

relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: We have demonstrated a broadly applicable approach to align, error-correct, group, and count sequences from orthogonal barcodes to quantify multimodal data such as cell surface protein abundance, to demultiplex samples, and to perform large-scale perturbation experiments. Our approach is fast, memory efficient, and extensible: orthogonal barcode quantifications can be obtained for numerous assays with variable sequence structure such the recently developed spatial RNA-seq assays (Srivatsan et al. 2021) and massively parallel reporter assays (Gordon et al. 2020). This allows future assay developers to avoid producing, validating, and maintaining software implementing ad hoc solutions. Moreover, some current methods are slow, have high memory requirements, and are specifically tailored for specific assays, which can result in batch effects when performing integrative analysis. Methods such as CITE-seq-Count offer extensibility features for different barcode strategies, but are slow and memory-intensive. The speed and efficiency of our approach enables reproducible single-cell analysis in the cloud with tools such as Google Colab. We anticipate that our framework for quantifying orthogonal barcoding assays will be useful as multimodal assays proliferate (Packer and Trapnell 2018), and that our quality control tool will help assay developers avoid pitfalls in barcode design and help practitioners quality control orthogonal barcode assays. Finally, while our approach is currently engineered to correct mismatch errors, robustness to other types of sequencing errors are possible via other methods that could readily be incorporated in our modular framework (Zorita, Cuscó, and Filion 2015; Booeshaghi et al. 2020; Milo S. Johnson, Sandeep Venkataram, Sergey Kryazhimskiy 2022).

Universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data
object.description: Large single-cell atlases depend on comparing datasets generated by many assays, so preprocessing must be consistent before biological interpretation begins. Existing workflows are often assay-specific, while read structures, barcode correction, and UMI/read counting differ across RNA, ATAC, protein, tags, and spatial modalities. cellatlas uses machine-readable seqspec files to configure modular tools for uniform preprocessing across nine datasets, modalities, and single-cell technologies.

relations.statement: This publication contains this grounded claim.

evidence.span: All preprocessing was performed by running the cellatlas command with the FASTQ files, associated seqspec, and reference sequences. The cellatlas commands can be found within each example folder in the cellatlas_info.json file. RNA and DNA reads were mapped to using the GRCh38 genome and GRCh38-108 annotation.

object.description: Large language models can extract text effectively but may hallucinate content absent from their source. Existing workflows support uniform preprocessing across multiple single-cell RNA-seq assays.

relations.statement: This publication is cited in support of this claim.

evidence.span: The importance of uniform preprocessing of single-cell genomics has been evident in the development of several workflows for multiple single-cell RNA-seq assays (Battenberg et al. 2022; He et al. 2022; Parekh et al. 2018; Tian et al. 2018). Here we have introduced an approach to uniform preprocessing that generalizes to many more assays and modalities by leveraging the modularity and flexibility of the kallisto and bustools programs, along with the seqspec standard for describing common elements in reads derived from single-cell genomics assays. Crucially, our approach enables quantitative comparisons both of distinct modalities within assays, as well as across technologies.

object.label: Algorithms for a Commons Cell Atlas
object.description: Cell atlases organize representative datasets, cell types, and marker genes across tissues. Manual duplicated curation, inconsistent preprocessing, and a lack of compatible tools make large atlases difficult to reprocess and update. The Commons Cell Atlas supplies validated infrastructure for fast iterative processing, including modular count-matrix workflows that support human and other organism atlases.

object.label: A machine-readable specification for genomics assays
object.description: Accurate preprocessing of genomics reads depends on knowing how biological and technical sequences are arranged in each library. Assay-specific scripts, divergent parameters, absent sequence annotations, and non-machine-readable library descriptions make uniform processing, comparison, and reanalysis difficult. Seqspec provides a YAML-based library specification and command-line tool that validates assay descriptions and generates technology strings for preprocessing tools.

object.label: Metadata retrieval from sequence databases with ffq
object.description: Public sequencing data are increasingly reused with new experiments, making metadata collation and raw-data acquisition essential. Existing metadata tools cover a limited set of databases, while user-uploaded sequencing metadata have little standardization. Ffq exploits shared database hierarchies to retrieve accession- or DOI-associated metadata and raw-data links as JSON and can extend to genomic databases with programmatic access.

relations.statement: Algorithms for a Commons Cell Atlas cites Metadata retrieval from sequence databases with ffq.

object.label: Modular, efficient and constant-memory single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing
object.description: Single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing quantifies transcript or gene abundance in individual cells. Experiments can span 10^6 to 10^10 reads, while existing workflows can require extensive time and disk space or memory that grows with dataset size. kallisto-bustools achieves near-optimal speed, constant memory, scaling to arbitrarily large datasets, Cell Ranger-consistent downstream analyses, and fast RNA-velocity analysis.

relations.statement: Algorithms for a Commons Cell Atlas cites Modular, efficient and constant-memory single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing.

object.label: Normalization for sampled count data
object.description: Genomics count normalization should stabilize technical variance, account for depth, and preserve within-cell abundance order. Common proportional-fitting and log workflows can retain depth dependence and conflate scaling with pseudocount choice. PFlog separates pseudocount choice from centered-log-ratio geometry, uniquely satisfies the three normalization desiderata, and outperformed alternatives across hundreds of single-cell RNA-seq datasets.

relations.statement: Algorithms for a Commons Cell Atlas cites Normalization for sampled count data.

object.label: Universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data
object.description: Large single-cell atlases depend on comparing datasets generated by many assays, so preprocessing must be consistent before biological interpretation begins. Existing workflows are often assay-specific, while read structures, barcode correction, and UMI/read counting differ across RNA, ATAC, protein, tags, and spatial modalities. cellatlas uses machine-readable seqspec files to configure modular tools for uniform preprocessing across nine datasets, modalities, and single-cell technologies.

relations.statement: Algorithms for a Commons Cell Atlas cites Universal preprocessing of single-cell genomics data.

object.label: Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data
object.description: Multivariate single-cell experiments can assay gene specificity across sex, tissue, age, genotype, and cell state. Existing specificity measures largely overlook multivariate structure or fail to decompose coherently across hierarchical partitions. Ember supplies three entropy-based metrics and is the only method shown to satisfy four desired specificity properties, revealing context-dependent markers, housekeeping genes, strain-driven cell-type switching, tissue-dominated mouse variation, and cell-type-dominated human PBMC variation.

object.label: Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto
object.description: Definitive full-length isoform quantification would extend RNA measurement beyond affordable gene-level short-read counts. Long-read data properties, isoform complexity, genetic variation, and much higher error rates create bioinformatic challenges. lr-kallisto makes pseudoalignment feasible for long reads while retaining efficiency and accurately quantifying biological and simulated data across error rates.

object.label: kallisto, bustools and kb-python for quantifying bulk, single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq
object.description: RNA-seq preprocessing must convert raw reads into expression measurements for bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus assays. The workflow must coordinate reference generation, mapping, quantification, and assay-specific read structures. kb-python reduces kallisto-bustools preprocessing to kb ref and kb count while supporting bulk, single-cell, single-nucleus, and joint nascent/mature-RNA analyses.

relations.statement: Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto cites kallisto, bustools and kb-python for quantifying bulk, single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq.

object.label: Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto
object.description: Long-read sequencing platforms can support full-length isoform quantification, but isoform complexity, genetic variation, and long-read error profiles create computational challenges. Efficient methods are needed to accurately associate long reads with transcripts of origin across current long-read data types. lr-kallisto accurately and efficiently quantifies long-read RNA-seq libraries, supports bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus data, benefits from exome capture, and uses less memory than compared long-read tools.

relations.statement: 2024-07-19 is a version of Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto.

object.label: Modular, efficient and constant-memory single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing
object.description: Single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing quantifies transcript or gene abundance in individual cells. Experiments can span 10^6 to 10^10 reads, while existing workflows can require extensive time and disk space or memory that grows with dataset size. kallisto-bustools achieves near-optimal speed, constant memory, scaling to arbitrarily large datasets, Cell Ranger-consistent downstream analyses, and fast RNA-velocity analysis.

relations.statement: Long-read sequencing transcriptome quantification with lr-kallisto cites Modular, efficient and constant-memory single-cell RNA-seq preprocessing.
